text:
Maya (People Ops): thanks everyone — quick follow-up from the all-hands. opening this thread for questions on reviews, leveling, promotions, and benefits. I'll triage and loop in folks. drop short questions here and we'll answer live.

Alex P: quick one — if someone is promoted in the calibration cycle, what's the effective date? can it be backdated to when they started acting up?

Maya (People Ops): good q. short answer: we generally set the effective date to the 1st of the month after the promotion approval. backdating is exceptional (e.g., documented acting-up duties + manager justification) and needs director + compensation sign-off. ping me the packet if you think it's a special case.

Jamal (Eng): also — what's the minimum time in role before someone is eligible for promotion? i've seen different answers.

Maya (People Ops): standard guideline is ~6 months in role for IC promotions, 9-12 months for manager track moves (exceptions: role change or major scope shift). managers should still provide evidence in the packet: impact, examples, peer feedback.

Devon (Manager): for calibration meetings — what's the expected prep? a template would help.

Maya (People Ops): yep. short checklist we ask for:
```
- 1-paragraph summary of impact
- 3 concrete examples + metrics if available
- Manager's recommendation (no/level-up/skip)
- Peer feedback summary
- Proposed title and new salary band (if recommending comp change)
```
attach to the calibration doc and share 48h before the meeting. i'll post the template after this thread.

Sara (Comp & Benefits): adding on comp timing: promotions approved in a cycle are processed within the next payroll window. salary changes go live the next pay period after effective date — expect ~2-6 weeks operationally depending on payroll cutoffs.

Alex P: are band ranges public? folks keep asking during 1:1s.

Sara (Comp & Benefits): we don't publish individual comp ranges company-wide, but managers can see band guidance in the comp tool. if you need a band for career conversations, ask your manager or ping comp@redwood. we can provide a summary range for the role.

hr-bot: link: /docs/people-ops/promo-calibration-template (shared) :link:

Devon (Manager): thanks — minor ask: any guidance for international hires and localized bands?

Maya (People Ops): yes — comp is localized by market. when you recommend an increase, note the candidate's location in the packet. comp will convert to local market band equivalent and flag any large delta for review.

Jamal (Eng): one more — performance improvement plans vs promotion freeze timing. if someone is on an active PIP, can they be considered for promotion?

Maya (People Ops): generally no — active PIP pauses promotion eligibility until completion and review. exceptions are very rare and need VP-level approval. that's to keep signals clear for the calibration panel.

Alex P: appreciated. can we get a short FAQ/one-pager for managers? sometimes the all-hands Q&A is too high level.

Maya (People Ops): on it. i'll draft a 1-pager with the checklist, timelines, and common scenarios and drop it here by EOD. if anything urgent, tag me. :thumbsup:

Sara (Comp & Benefits): tagging compensation owners — if you want anonymized band examples to show during 1:1s, DM me.

Maya (People Ops): closing note — if you emailed escalations to people-ops@redwood, i'll surface them in the calibration queue. thanks for the questions.
